description: Authenticated per-user invalidation stream. Clients subscribe once per login; the backend fanouts targeted events for discovery surfaces and identity-bundle changes. Matches the C# UserEventBroadcaster + DiscoveryAudience pipeline and the Rust user_events consumer.

discovery.invalidated.notes: `surfaces` is a non-empty array of DiscoverySurface slugs from the list above. `roomId` scopes room-chat and room-tasks invalidations to the changed room; it is omitted for global discovery invalidations. Clients refresh the named authoritative projections.

user.deviceListChanged.notes: Signals that `userId` has rotated their signed device list to a positive `generation`, triggering an identity-bundle refetch and chain-forward pin-store verification. Non-positive generations are protocol violations; `user.identityLifecycleChanged` is the sole ordered withdrawal and re-enrollment authority.

user.identityLifecycleChanged.notes: Latest-wins identity lifecycle authority. `identityRevision` is strictly increasing per target user and orders resets/re-enrollments. `state` is `withdrawn` with null `incarnationId` and generation 0, or `enrolled` with a UUIDv7 incarnation and generation >= 1. Clients persist the highest revision independently of pins, ignore lower/equal revisions, clear stale-incarnation trust, and never background-TOFU a new incarnation. The /me/events priming snapshot streams one current row per historically exposed target before buffered live events.

user.deviceLinkSnapshot.notes: Durable priming frame sent before buffered live device-link events. `requests` contains every unexpired pending enrollment request for the authenticated user. Clients replace their pending-link projection from this snapshot, then apply requested/resolved events incrementally.

user.deviceLinkRequested.notes: A new device has initiated an RFC 8628-style enrollment for this user. Every enrolled device of the same user receives this and surfaces a banner prompting the user to approve on one of their existing devices. `deviceLabel` is a UX hint (not cryptographically trusted) so the user recognises their own request. Visual match of `userCode` against what the new device displays is the real out-of-band check.

user.deviceLinkResolved.notes: A previously-broadcast link request has finished. `outcome` is `approved` (the user approved on another device — dismiss the banner) or `cancelled` (the initiating device cancelled — dismiss the banner). Any enrolled device that raised a banner for `userCode` drops it on receipt.
